conventions.convention: A ≈ B means that a bijection A → B exists; A ≼ B means that an injection A → B exists; A ≺ B means A ≼ B and not A ≈ B.
The naturals are the von Neumann naturals, starting at 0 = ∅. Their additively defined order satisfies m < n iff m ∈ n and m ≤ n iff m ⊆ n.

Finite means equinumerous with a natural number; countably infinite means equinumerous with ℕ; countable alone means at most countable, including finite and empty sets; uncountable means not at most countable.
The surjection-from-ℕ criterion assumes a nonempty target and permits repetitions. Its reverse direction uses the least preimage index, without choice.
ACω selects from every ℕ-indexed family of nonempty sets, without restricting the sizes of its members.
DC applies to a nonempty set with an entire relation and provides an ℕ-indexed sequence from a prescribed starting point. Terms may repeat; this is not necessarily an order-theoretic chain.
AC2 allows arbitrary set-indexed families of pairs; ACω,2 restricts the index set to ω; ACω,fin allows ω-indexed nonempty finite sets without supplied orderings.
The countable-union theorem explicitly assumes ACω and spends it on simultaneous selection of surjections onto the nonempty family members. The two-set union arguments do not invoke it.
The real root bound counts distinct real roots of a finite coefficient list with nonzero leading coefficient. Degree 0 is allowed and has an empty root set.

Real algebraic numbers are roots of nonzero integer coefficient lists, with the integers embedded through ℤ → ℚ → ℝ. Invalid decoded lists use the constant polynomial 1; finite real root sets receive their unique increasing listings.

load_bearing.statement: A is finite if A ≈ n for some n ∈ ℕ; countably infinite if A ≈ ℕ; at most countable if finite or countably infinite; uncountable if not at most countable.
Let A be a nonempty set. Then A is at most countable if and only if there is a surjection s : ℕ → A. From any such surjection, j(a) = min{k ∈ ℕ : s(k) = a} is an injection A → ℕ, without choice.
ℕ × ℕ ≈ ℕ. J(m,n) = 2^m(2n+1) is a bijection onto ℕ ∖ {0}; composing with the inverse successor gives a bijection onto ℕ.
Let A be at most countable and B ⊆ A. Then B is at most countable. A subset S ⊆ ℕ is finite if bounded above, and countably infinite if not bounded above.
Let ℝ be a complete ordered field. Then ℝ is uncountable: there is no surjection ℕ → ℝ, so ℝ is neither finite nor countably infinite.
Let A and B be sets with A ≼ B and B ≼ A. Then A ≈ B. The proof uses no choice principle.

For every n ∈ ℕ there is no injection σ(n) → n; if m < n there is no injection n → m; equinumerous naturals are equal; ℕ is equinumerous with no natural; and no natural is equinumerous with a proper subset of itself.
ℕ is transitive; for m,n ∈ ℕ, m < n iff m ∈ n, m ≤ n iff m ⊆ n, n < σ(n), m < σ(n) iff m ≤ n, and 0 ≤ n with 0 ∈ n whenever n ≠ 0.
In ZF, AC ⇒ DC ⇒ ACω ⇒ ACω,fin ⇒ ACω,2, and AC ⇒ AC2. DC includes a prescribed initial point.
Let d ∈ ℕ and a₀,…,a_d ∈ ℝ with a_d ≠ 0. For P(x) = Σ(k=0,…,d) a_k x^k, its real zero set Z satisfies Z ≈ m for some m ∈ ℕ with m ≤ d. For d = 0, Z = ∅.
A nonempty F ⊆ ℝ is finite iff F = {a₀,…,a_n} for some n ∈ ℕ and real entries. Consequently every nonempty finite subset of ℝ has a maximum and a minimum.
For every set A there is no surjection A → P(A); consequently A ≺ P(A).

concerns.concern: The second Remark ends, “Countability is not preserved by infinite products of any kind.” Read literally, “of any kind” overstates the demonstrated counterexample: an infinite product of singleton sets is a singleton. The preceding binary-product example correctly establishes that infinite products need not preserve countability; the final wording should express that general failure without a universal exclusion.

The Objective says, “The rational enumeration and the algebraic-number item also use the finite-sum and natural-power interfaces of [[roots-and-rational-powers]].” The explicit rational enumeration uses the natural-number pairing arithmetic of thm-n-cross-n-countable, not def-finite-sum or the real-base powers of def-integer-power. The root-bound and algebraic-number items do use those roots-page interfaces. Align this page-level dependency description with the actual consumers.

alerts.finding: F2 attributes thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology to “a bounded-below constructible coefficient complex F of lower bound a.” The opened supplier's Statement instead requires “F ∈ D^b_c(X;k) over a field.” Having a cochain lower bound within that bounded category does not broaden the supplier to arbitrary bounded-below constructible complexes. The quoted F2 interface is therefore stronger than its source. The actual constant rational coefficient used in this proof satisfies the supplier's bounded hypothesis, so this finding concerns the overstrong cited fact rather than that application.
